Suppose we like to calculate P(H|E, F) and we have no conditional independence
information. Which of the following sets of numbers are sufficient for the calculation?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - P(E, F), P(H), P(E, F|H)

questions.stem_text:
Consider the Bayesian network given below. How many independent parameters would we need
if we made no assumptions about independence or conditional independence H -> U <- P <- W?
The number of test examples needed to get statistically significant results should be _

options.A: Larger if the error rate is larger.
options.B: Larger if the error rate is smaller.
options.C: Smaller if the error rate is smaller.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - Larger if the error rate is smaller.

questions.stem_text:
Which of the following best describes the joint probability distribution P(X, Y, Z) for
the given Bayes net. X <- Y -> Z?

options.A: P(X, Y, Z) = P(Y) * P(X|Y) * P(Z|Y)
options.B: P(X, Y, Z) = P(X) * P(Y|X) * P(Z|Y)
options.C: P(X, Y, Z) = P(Z) * P(X|Z) * P(Y|Z)
options.D: P(X, Y, Z) = P(X) * P(Y) * P(Z)

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - P(X, Y, Z) = P(Y) * P(X|Y) * P(Z|Y)
